title: Best Running Socks UK
short: Merino, synthetic and blister-preventing running socks compared by fabric, cushioning and fit.
intro: The right running sock is the cheapest way to avoid blisters and soggy feet. This guide compares socks that repeatedly show up in independent runner testing, covering fabric, cushioning, height and the conditions each one suits.

guide.q: Merino wool or synthetic running socks?
guide.a: Merino wool controls odour well and feels comfortable across a wide temperature range. Synthetic socks tend to dry faster and often cost less. Many of the best socks blend both.

guide.q: What height of running sock should I choose?
guide.a: No-show and low socks suit road running in warm weather. Crew and mid-height socks add protection against debris on trails and warmth in cold weather.

guide.q: How can I stop blisters when running?
guide.a: Choose a snug sock that does not bunch or slide, avoid cotton-heavy fabrics that hold sweat, and consider toe-sock designs if you get blisters between toes. Break in new socks and shoes before a long run.

guide.q: How often should I replace running socks?
guide.a: Replace them when the cushioning flattens, the fabric thins or holes appear. Frequent runners often go through a pair every few months.
